full_caption: Georgiana Marchetti-Doyle, Appellant, v. Theodora Umberton, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Georgiana Marchetti-Doyle claims title by adverse possession to a 12.5-acre wooded tract adjoining 2426 Old Quarry Turnpike, Stillwater, CW, of which Theodora Umberton is the record owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The trial court found the elements satisfied as to 22.6 acres and not satisfied as to the remainder, which lay beyond any fence or posted line. That allocation is not clearly erroneous.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Georgiana Marchetti-Doyle posted the tract against trespass in 2005, cut and sold standing timber in 2017 and 2026, and maintained a hunting camp on the northeast quarter continuously thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Hostility does not require ill will. It requires only that the possession be without the record owner's permission and inconsistent with the owner's title. A claimant's mistaken belief as to the true line does not defeat hostility in this State.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Continuity is broken by an entry of the record owner made with intent to reclaim possession. The single survey visit by Theodora Umberton's agent in 2038, unaccompanied by any assertion of possession, did not interrupt the running of the statute.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Payment of property taxes is not an independent element in this jurisdiction but is evidence bearing on the notoriety of the claim. Georgiana Marchetti-Doyle paid taxes assessed against the tract for 9 of the 10 years in question.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Adverse possession requires possession that is actual, open and notorious, exclusive, hostile, and continuous for the statutory period of 10 years. Each element must be established by clear and convincing evidence.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Possession is 'actual' where the claimant uses the land as an ordinary owner of similar land would use it. For wooded acreage, selective timbering, posting, and seasonal recreational use may suffice where cultivation would not be expected.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Tacking is permitted between successive possessors in privity. Georgiana Marchetti-Doyle may tack the 9 years of possession by its predecessor, whose deed purported to convey the disputed tract, to satisfy the statutory term.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Color of title is not required where the claim rests on actual occupancy, but it enlarges the claim to the full extent of the described premises rather than the portion actually occupied.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Land held by a municipality for a public purpose is not subject to adverse possession. The 16-foot strip within the platted right of way is therefore excluded from any judgment in Georgiana Marchetti-Doyle's favor.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: Affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded for entry of a decree describing the vested tract by metes and bounds consistent with the surveyor's Exhibit B.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ACTS OF POSSESSION RELIED UPON
sections.text: Claimant relies upon the following acts, each continuing from the date shown through the date of filing: posting of the perimeter against trespass beginning in 2005; commercial timber harvest in 2017 and 2026; construction and continuous seasonal use of a hunting camp; annual maintenance of the interior access track; and payment of the real property taxes assessed against the tract for 9 of the 10 years preceding this claim.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — EXCLUSIONS FROM CLAIM
sections.text: This claim expressly excludes: (a) any land held by the municipality or the State for a public purpose, including the 16-foot platted right of way; (b) any land subject to a recorded easement, as to which Claimant asserts no interest inconsistent with the easement; and (c) any subsurface mineral estate previously severed of record.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — QUIET TITLE RELIEF REQUESTED
sections.text: Claimant requests a decree quieting title in Claimant as against Respondent and all persons claiming under Respondent, describing the vested tract by metes and bounds, directing the Recorder to index the decree against both parcels, and awarding costs. Claimant does not seek damages for the period of possession.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Indemnity
sections.text: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from all claims, damages and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of that party's use of the subject premises or breach of this instrument, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the party seeking indemnity. This clause survives termination.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Calloway.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Severability
sections.text: If any provision of this instrument is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable, and if it cannot be so reformed it shall be severed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.
